title: SECTION 1, UNIT 1
subtitle: Differentiate foundational generic drug pairs (buPROPion/busPIRone, hydrALAZINE/hydrOXYzine, predniSONE/prednisoLONE) using Tall Man lettering.
unitMessage: ISMP & FDA Foundational Look-Alike Generic Confusions

lasaPairs.feature: Confusion between an antidepressant/smoking cessation aid and an anxiolytic; risk of seizure (bupropion overdose) or untreated anxiety/depression.
Severe hypotension from accidental hydralazine, or unintended central nervous system sedation from hydroxyzine.
Dosing errors in pediatric/hepatic failure populations where conversion from prednisone to active prednisolone is impaired.
Excessive sedation, hypotension, unmanaged acute pain, or increased risk of serotonin syndrome.
Severe bradycardia and hypotension from clonidine, or central nervous system depression and dependence issues from clonazepam.
Potency and duration differences leading to oversedation, respiratory depression, or altered seizure threshold.
Agranulocytosis, severe orthostatic hypotension, seizures, and metabolic side effects from accidental clozapine administration.
Uncontrolled pain or inflammation vs. psychiatric destabilization, QT prolongation, or serotonin toxicity.
Hydromorphone is 4 to 7 times more potent than morphine; administering hydromorphone at morphine doses frequently results in fatal respiratory arrest.
Hemodynamic instability, dangerous tachycardia, or inappropriate peripheral vasoconstriction/vasodilation in critical care.
Potency mismatch leading to either inadequate analgesia or opioid overdose and hypoventilation.
Prolonged, severe hypoglycemia, especially in elderly patients or those with renal impairment given glyburide.
Lactic acidosis and GI distress vs. untreated anaerobic infection or disulfiram-like ethanol reaction.
